title: Determination 2024/041: Refusal to grant building consent for work to decommission an automatic sprinkler system in a cold store (fire load, warning system, fire rating)
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Christchurch City Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992); clauses C3.6 and C3.8 applied. No Acceptable Solution edition is named in the text read.

facts.text: Two adjoining cold-store warehouses (Units A and B) on the site are fire separated by concrete fire walls and share a plant room, connected by a partially covered walkway.
Unit A (built 1996) is a single-level racked cold store of about 3,000 m2, made primarily of expanded polystyrene panels. Its warehouse area has a dry-pipe sprinkler system.
Unit B (built 1998, extended 2001) is a single-level cold store of about 4,000 m2 with racking. It has no sprinkler system and has a manual call-point fire alarm system.
When the dry-pipe system was inspected, the in-rack sprinklers were found to be iced up.

The owner applied for building consent BCN/2019/4930. The proposal was first to reconfigure the sprinkler system and then to convert parts of it to function as an automatic thermal detection system, with the in-rack dry-pipe systems disestablished and wet-pipe sprinklers kept in ambient areas.
The authority refused the consent because of outstanding issues on fire load, the proposed replacement warning system, and fire-rating requirements.
The determination consulted Fire and Emergency New Zealand under section 170(a).
